documents.body: No problem, cancelled. Just message us when you have a sense of your fall schedule and we'll find a morning.

documents.title: Breathing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I never rebooked my physical, sorry. But I'd like to come in about my breathing. I've been getting winded way more than I should for a while now and it's not getting better. Not an emergency. Any morning next week works.

documents.title: RE: Breathing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you wrote. Tuesday 12/5 at 7:40 works on my end - front desk will confirm. If you get chest pain, or you're short of breath sitting still, call me rather than waiting.

results.test: Alpha 1 antitrypsin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

reports.text: CHEST, PA AND LATERAL. Indication: 34-year-old man, never smoker, 14 months of progressive dyspnea, SpO2 91%. Comparison: none. Findings: The lungs are hyperlucent. There are bullous changes at both lung bases. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size is normal. Mediastinal contours are normal. Osseous structures are unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Hyperlucent lungs with bilateral basal bullous changes.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Declan comes in about his breathing. Says it started creeping up a little over a year ago, around October of last year, and has slowly gotten worse. Now one flight of stairs leaves him winded, and a few minutes of walking fast does the same. Tired more than he used to be. At work he's stopped demonstrating drills for the kids and just talks them through it, which bothers him. Dry cough, mild, most days. Some wheezing now and then, mostly with exertion. No fever, no chest pain, no leg swelling, no hemoptysis. No orthopnea.

Never smoked. His partner started smoking again over a year ago and does smoke in the house. Drinks rarely. No work exposures he can think of beyond gym dust.

Family: father with emphysema at 42 who died of cirrhosis at 48; paternal uncle with COPD; paternal grandmother with cirrhosis of unknown cause.

Meds none. NKDA.

Exam: T 36.8, HR 82, RR 18, BP 122/78, SpO2 91% RA. Weight down about 3 kg from last summer's physical. Not in distress at rest. Scattered end-expiratory wheezes, rhonchi at both bases. Heart regular, no murmur. No JVD. Abdomen soft, no liver edge. No clubbing, no edema.

A/P: 34 y/o never smoker with 14 months of progressive exertional dyspnea, cough, wheeze, and a resting sat of 91%. With his father's early emphysema and two relatives with liver disease, I am worried about alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
- CXR PA/lat today, walked over to imaging
- Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level, CBC, CMP drawn here
- Full PFTs with lung volumes and DLCO, ordered
- Will call him when PFTs are back to put it together

Addendum 15:40: CXR reviewed - hyperlucent lungs, bullous change at both bases. Fits the concern above. Pt aware by phone, PFTs set for 12/12.

documents.title: Blood test result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Declan, your alpha-1 antitrypsin level came back low at 24 (normal is roughly 100 to 190). Your blood count and the kidney and liver tests were fine. A low level like this goes along with what the X-ray showed. I'd like the breathing tests on Tuesday before we talk through what it means - I'll call you once I have them.

documents.title: RE: Blood test result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok. I looked it up, is this the thing that runs in families? My dad's lungs were bad young. Talk Tuesday.

reports.study: Pulmonary function tests (spirometry, lung volumes, DLCO)
reports.text: PULMONARY FUNCTION LABORATORY REPORT. Referring: primary care. Tests performed: spirometry with pre and post bronchodilator, lung volumes by plethysmography, single-breath diffusing capacity. Effort and reproducibility acceptable. Interpretation: Obstructive ventilatory defect. Diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide is decreased. Results tables attached to the original report.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive ventilatory pattern with decreased DLCO.

documents.title: Pulmonary function test report
documents.author: pulmonary function lab
documents.body: Hospital pulmonary function laboratory. Date of test: 12/12/2023. Patient: Declan Merrill, DOB 05/09/1989. Allergies: NKDA. Obstructive ventilatory defect with decreased diffusing capacity. Interpreting physician signature on file. Received electronically, routed to PCP.

orders.reason: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with basal bullous changes and obstruction

documents.title: Results discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt at lunch, ~20 min. Went over the pieces: basal bullous change on CXR, obstruction with a low DLCO on yesterday's PFTs, AAT level 24, in a 34-year-old who has never smoked and whose father had emphysema at 42. This is alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency affecting his lungs. Explained it is inherited and that the exact type is worked out with genetic testing, which pulmonology will handle along with the question of treatment.

Referral to pulmonology placed, marked soon.
Asked that his partner not smoke in the house or the car at all - he says she's already offered to take it outside. Keep drinking to a minimum, liver can be involved in this condition too. Flu and COVID already done this fall.
He asked about his school duties - fine to keep teaching and coaching, pace himself, no need to push through breathlessness.
He'll let me know when pulmonology calls.

documents.title: Referral processed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pulmonology referral faxed with the 12/5 note, CXR, AAT result and PFT report. Their office scheduled him for 2/6/24. Pt notified by portal. Insurance does not require a referral number for this plan.

documents.title: Saw the lung doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just closing the loop - I saw pulmonology back on Feb 6. They did more breathing tests, didn't start me on anything, and want to see me again in about a year and a half unless it gets worse. Did they send you anything?

documents.title: RE: Saw the lung doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me - nothing has come over yet. We'll ask them for the note. Keep me posted on how you're doing in the meantime.

documents.title: Records request - pulmonology
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Requested consult note and PFTs from 2/6/24 pulmonology visit. Faxed request with signed release.

documents.title: Records request - second attempt
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Nothing received from pulmonology for the 2/6 visit. Re-faxed request, left a message with their records line. Will flag for PCP if still nothing.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35M, physical. Problem: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, dx 12/2023.

Breathing about where it was last winter - stairs still wind him, he paces himself at practice. Cough comes and goes. Saw pulmonology 2/2024, no treatment started, next visit planned for fall 2025; their note never reached us despite two requests. Partner smokes outside only now.

Meds none. NKDA. Alcohol: a drink or two a month.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 93% RA. Thin, comfortable at rest. Breath sounds mildly diminished both sides, no wheeze today, no crackles. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly. No clubbing or edema.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
- AATD with lung involvement: stable by history. Keep the pulmonology follow-up. Pneumococcal vaccine today given chronic lung disease.
- Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids. Flu and updated COVID today.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your bloodwork from Tuesday is all in the normal range, including the liver numbers and cholesterol. Arm soreness from three shots in one morning should be gone in a day or two.
